BiblicalUsage: To dwell, the Aramaic word for where men and beasts live, used when Nebuchadnezzar is told that wherever the children of men dwell, God has given them into his hand. The great tree of his dream had fair leaves and fruit for all, and the beasts of the field dwelt under its shadow.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe dwelling is a gift God gives and a trust He measures, because the tree that sheltered the beasts was cut down when its branches grew proud. Where I dwell, and under whose shadow, is a question God asks of kings and of me.
RelatedEvents: Nebuchadnezzar's Dream of the Image; Nebuchadnezzar's Humbling
